messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated pool dp-8791 (tenant: Northforge) reporting GPU exhaustion and request queue growth. Severity: P1. Triggered at 2024-04-05T10:55:01Z. Paging on-call SRE.

maya-sre: got the page, on it — pulling metrics now.

maya-sre: dashboards show GPU util ~98% across all nodes, queue length jumping, recent spike in token throughput from northforge-prod. Autoscaler hit max_instances=4 and refused to scale further.

alex-oncall: confirmed. Heap of small real-time requests plus a few big batch retrain jobs started by tenant's ops team. Customer reported 502s in support channel (jamie-cs).

jamie-cs: Northforge account manager DMed me, they're seeing ~60% request failures since 10:52 UTC. They've flagged as P1 and want immediate mitigation. I can join call if needed.

chris-plat: we can do an emergency burst from shared capacity but policy requires platform lead approval for >1.5x. @alex-oncall can you authorize? We should also consider a temporary tenant-level throttle or model fallback to reduce memory pressure.

alex-oncall: I approve emergency burst up to 2x for 30m to buy time. Please document the window and reason.

maya-sre: initiating mitigations now: 1) throttle low-priority tenant routes 2) suspend tenant batch jobs 3) request burst to shared pool. Running commands:
```
# throttle low priority routes
redwoodctl routes update --tenant northforge --rate-limit "low:50r/s"

# suspend batch jobs
redwoodctl jobs suspend --tenant northforge --label jobclass=batch --reason "Emergency mitigation - GPU exhaustion"

# request burst
redwoodctl pool burst --pool dp-8791 --to shared-pool --gpus 2 --duration 30m --reason "Emergency burst - P1 enterprise"
```

deploy-bot: Burst request queued. Request id br-5531. Awaiting provisioning.

chris-plat: provisioning now — allocating 2 GPUs from shared-pool to dp-8791 (br-5531). ETA ~90s.

deploy-bot: br-5531 accepted. Nodes provisioning: node-az1-gtx-09, node-az2-gtx-02.

maya-sre: while that comes up, enabling model fallback rule for tenant to fall back to quantized variant to reduce memory:
```
# per-tenant model override
redwoodctl tenant-config set northforge --model-fallback "llama-13b-q4" --apply-immediately true
```

sylvia-eng: I'll push a conservative routing change so critical customer traffic hits GPUs that are already warmed with KV cache. Rolling config to route priority=high -> warmed-nodes.

alex-oncall: handoff plan: I will take over on-call from maya at 11:05 UTC to run the stabilization and post-incident follow-ups. Maya, can you confirm outstanding actions?

maya-sre: handing off to @alex-oncall at 11:05 UTC. Outstanding: 1) confirm br-5531 successfully attached and reduced queue 2) monitor error rate and latency for 20m 3) create QE ticket for permanent surge limit change 4) coordinate with Jamie for customer comms.

chris-plat: br-5531 shows allocated and nodes joined the pool. Immediate drop in queue depth observed, GPU util down to ~70% on new nodes.

maya-sre: error rate dropped from 60%->12% within 3 minutes. 95th latency from 1.8s->850ms. Continuing to observe.

jamie-cs: I told the AM we initiated an emergency burst and have throttled non-essential traffic. AM is drafting an incident note to send to Northforge with ETA for full remediation. They asked for a timeline for permanent quota increase.

alex-oncall: marking incident as contained for now. Still in mitigation window. Actions for follow-up: - create postmortem (owner: maya-sre) - QE ticket for quota increase (owner: chris-plat) - engineering task to add autoscaler alert for cap-hit (owner: sylvia-eng) - customer follow-up call (owner: jamie-cs)

chris-plat: opened ticket QE-4321 to request permanent surge limit increase for dp-8791 (+2 GPUs) and to review autoscaler cap guardrails. Link: <https://console.redwood.infra/tickets/QE-4321>

deploy-bot: br-5531 scheduled to expire at 11:25 UTC (30m). Extend if still needed via redwoodctl or coordinate with platform.

maya-sre: note — we also discovered tenant batch job config didn't have proper throttle; adding an action item to require per-tenant batch rate limit.

alex-oncall: I'll stay on the incident until we hit 11:30 UTC and ensure metrics are stable. If recovery holds, we'll end incident and start postmortem.

jamie-cs: AM confirmed they want a follow-up call at 14:00 UTC. I'll set calendar invite after incident resolved.

incident-bot: STATUS UPDATE: mitigation applied, error rate falling, burst active. Incident state: ACTIVE -> CONTAINED at 2024-04-05T11:03:20Z.

alex-oncall: final check at 11:30 UTC: queue stable, GPU util baseline ~55-65%, error rate <2% for 15m. Proceeding to drain burst, will leave model-fallback in place for 2 hours as precaution.

chris-plat: draining br-5531 now.

deploy-bot: br-5531 drained and nodes returned to shared-pool.

alex-oncall: incident RESOLVED at 2024-04-05T11:33:20Z. Postmortem owner assigned to maya-sre, timeframe 48h. QE-4321 linked. Jamie to confirm customer comms.

jamie-cs: AM confirmed receipt and appreciated the quick action. They requested to be included in postmortem.

maya-sre: adding follow-ups to ops-tracking board: "tenant-burst-policy-review", "autoscaler-cap-alert", "tenant-batch-throttle-requirement".

sylvia-eng: will triage autoscaler alert work with priority P2.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED. Summary: dedicated pool dp-8791 experienced tenant-driven GPU exhaustion; emergency burst + throttles + model fallback mitigated customer impact. Follow-ups created: QE-4321, ops-tracking items.
